events.title: FAO adopts term "community forestry"
events.description: FAO originally adopted the term "community forestry" as an umbrella term for any situation that intimately involves local people in a forestry activity.
events.supporting_text: FAO (1978, p. 1) originally adopted the term "community forestry" as an umbrella term for "any situation which intimately involves local people in a forestry activity".

significance.justification: Standardising terminology shapes discourse and acceptance of community‑based approaches.
significance.supporting_text: FAO (1978, p. 1) originally adopted the term “community forestry” as an umbrella term…

events.title: FAO defines "social forestry"
events.description: FAO published a definition of "social forestry", a term used interchangeably with community forestry by some and to describe a narrower set of activities such as woodlot establishment for deforestation mitigation and fuelwood provision.
events.supporting_text: "Social forestry" is used by some as interchangeable with community forestry and by others to describe a much narrower spectrum of activities such as establishment of woodlots to address deforestation and provide fuelwood (FAO, 1991).

significance.justification: The undefined use of “social forestry” highlights existing confusion that hampers coherent action.
significance.supporting_text: the concurrent emergence of the term “social forestry”, for which no clear definition exists, began a degree of confusion

events.title: FAO defines participatory forestry
events.description: FAO provided a definition of participatory forestry, describing it as processes and mechanisms that enable people with a direct stake in forest resources to participate in decision‑making across all aspects of forest management, including policy formulation.
events.supporting_text: FAO (2012b) has defined participatory forestry as: "processes and mechanisms which enable people with a direct stake in forest resources to be part of decision-making in all aspects of forest management, including policy formulation processes".

significance.justification: Definition explicitly links people to decision‑making, enabling collective management.
significance.supporting_text: FAO (2012b) has defined participatory forestry as: “processes and mechanisms which enable people … to be part of decision‑making”

events.title: FAO review of 25 years of community forestry
events.description: FAO published a comprehensive review covering 25 years of community forestry, providing a historical overview and analysis of the evolution of community‑based forestry regimes.
events.supporting_text: This follows the approach taken in FAO's 2001 review of 25 years of community forestry (Arnold, 2001).

significance.justification: The review synthesises four decades of experience, exposing pathways for broader transformation.
significance.supporting_text: This publication looks back over the past 40 years of CBF implementation, reviewing the extent to which it has become a major forest management modality

events.title: FAO regional assessment of community forestry in Asia
events.description: FAO released a regional assessment documenting the status and trends of community forestry across Asian countries.
events.supporting_text: Both FAO and the Rights and Resources Initiative (RRI) have carried out regional and global assessments to chart these changes (see e.g. FAO, 2006a for Asia; ...

significance.justification: Shows the substantial increase of forest area under CBF, indicating current trends.
significance.supporting_text: These reports have highlighted a substantial increase in the area of forest land under various CBF regimes during the past two decades

events.title: FAO regional assessment of community forestry in Africa
events.description: FAO published a regional assessment that examined the expansion and impact of community forestry programmes throughout African nations.
events.supporting_text: ... FAO, 2008 for Africa ...

significance.justification: Documents the present scale of CBF in Africa, revealing existing conditions.
significance.supporting_text: These reports have highlighted a substantial increase in the area of forest land under various CBF regimes during the past two decades

events.title: FAO regional assessment of community forestry in Eastern Europe
events.description: FAO issued a regional review focusing on community forestry developments and policy implementation in Eastern European countries.
events.supporting_text: ... FAO, 2012a for Eastern Europe ...

significance.justification: Provides evidence of current CBF coverage in Eastern Europe.
significance.supporting_text: These reports have highlighted a substantial increase in the area of forest land under various CBF regimes during the past two decades

events.title: White and Martin global review of community forestry
events.description: White and Martin produced a global review that synthesized evidence on community forestry programmes worldwide.
events.supporting_text: White and Martin, 2002

significance.justification: A global synthesis that makes the worldwide state of CBF visible.
significance.supporting_text: White and Martin, 2002 and RRI, 2014a for global reviews

events.title: Rights and Resources Initiative (RRI) global review of community forestry
events.description: RRI released a global review that charted changes in community forestry regimes across the world.
events.supporting_text: RRI, 2014a for global reviews

significance.justification: RRI’s assessment maps global CBF changes, exposing current patterns.
significance.supporting_text: Both FAO and the Rights and Resources Initiative (RRI) have carried out regional and global assessments to chart these changes

events.title: Menton and Cronkleton review of CBF initiatives in the Peruvian Amazon
events.description: Menton and Cronkleton conducted a review of community‑based forestry initiatives in the Peruvian Amazon, concluding that comprehensive assessments of programme effectiveness were lacking.
events.supporting_text: Menton and Cronkleton (2014, p. 1), following a review of CBF initiatives in the Peruvian Amazon, reached the conclusion that "even though there has been a great deal of research documenting forest use by rural people ... We couldn't find any comprehensive assessments of the effectiveness of existing programmes to promote community forestry or benefit local people."

significance.justification: The review points out the lack of comprehensive effectiveness assessments.
significance.supporting_text: We couldn’t find any comprehensive assessments of the effectiveness of existing programmes to promote community forestry

events.title: Publication of "Forestry for local community development"
events.description: Seminal FAO paper that marked the first formal recognition of community‑based forestry as a distinct modality of forest management.
events.supporting_text: The emergence, growth and evolution of community-based forestry as a formally recognizable modality of forest management can be traced back to the seminal paper Forestry for local community development (FAO, 1978).

events.title: Eighth World Forestry Congress in Jakarta
events.description: International forestry congress that adopted the theme “Forests for People,” highlighting the link between forest management and human well‑being.
events.supporting_text: In the same year, the eighth World Forestry Congress in Jakarta carried the theme "Forests for People".

events.title: Emergence of smallholder and community‑based forestry
events.description: A multi‑year process during the 1970s and 1980s in which smallholder and community‑based forestry arose as an alternative to the dominant forest‑industry development model, driven by rising deforestation and land‑degradation pressures in developing countries.
events.supporting_text: During the 1970s and 1980s, smallholder and community-based forestry emerged in response partly to a perceived failure of the forest industry development model to lead to socioeconomic development, and partly to the increasing rate of deforestation and forest land degradation in developing countries (Gilmour, King and Hobley, 1989).

events.title: Implementation of new tree‑growing and forest‑management programmes
events.description: By the late 1970s, a series of programmes and projects were launched to support tree‑growing and forest management at farm and community levels, aiming to integrate forestry into broader agricultural systems.
events.supporting_text: By the end of the 1970s, new programmes and projects were being put in place to provide support to tree growing and forest management at both farm and community levels.

events.title: Initiation of forestry for local community development
events.description: Beginning of forestry activities aimed at supporting local community development in response to the fuelwood crisis and the failure of the forest industry development model.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1970s. Events: Fuelwood crisis, Failure of forest industry development model to sustain forests and meet community needs. Response: Initiation of forestry for local community development

significance.justification: The initiative creates a community‑led production model that enables local agency and aligns forest use with regeneration goals.
significance.supporting_text: Initiation of forestry for local community development

events.title: Establishment of fuelwood plantations (top‑down approach)
events.description: Creation of fuelwood plantations, largely driven by top‑down policies, as a response to the fuelwood crisis; many of these plantations later failed.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1970s. Response: ... Establishment of fuelwood plantations (generally top-down); many failed

significance.justification: The top‑down plantation effort, noted as largely failing, highlights a prevailing policy that did not respect ecological limits.
significance.supporting_text: Establishment of fuelwood plantations (generally top‑down); many failed

events.title: Pilot projects testing CBF modalities in different settings
events.description: Implementation of pilot projects that experimented with community‑based forestry approaches to address large‑scale deforestation and environmental degradation.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1980s. Events: Large‑scale deforestation; environmental degradation ... Response: Pilot projects tested CBF modalities in different settings to address environmental concerns

significance.justification: Pilot projects explore varied CBF approaches, indicating pathways for broader systemic transformation.
significance.supporting_text: Pilot projects tested CBF modalities in different settings

events.title: Emergence of people’s participation and bottom‑up development
events.description: Development of participatory, bottom‑up approaches in forest sector reforms, emphasizing local community involvement.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1980s. Response: ... Emergence of "people's participation" and bottom‑up development

significance.justification: The emergence signals a shift toward inclusive, locally driven decision‑making that can mobilize collective effort.
significance.supporting_text: Emergence of “people’s participation” and bottom‑up development

events.title: Focus on sustainable forest management (SFM) and livelihoods as CBF objectives
events.description: Shift toward integrating sustainable forest management and livelihood improvement into community‑based forestry goals, following the rise of the sustainable development paradigm and recognition of indigenous rights.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1990s. Events: Sustainable development paradigm, Recognition of indigenous peoples' rights. Response: Focus on SFM and livelihoods as CBF objectives

significance.justification: Linking SFM with livelihoods shows how ecological and social goals can co‑evolve, opening a route to systemic change.
significance.supporting_text: Focus on SFM and livelihoods as CBF objectives

events.title: Establishment of CBF regimes that formalize indigenous peoples' rights to manage forests
events.description: Creation of formal community‑based forestry arrangements that legally recognize indigenous peoples' rights to forest management.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1990s. Response: Establishment of CBF regimes that formalize indigenous peoples' rights to manage forests

significance.justification: Formalizing indigenous rights empowers communities to manage forests, strengthening collective stewardship.
significance.supporting_text: Establishment of CBF regimes that formalize indigenous peoples’ rights to manage forests

events.title: Expansion of CBF across all regions
events.description: Geographic spread of community‑based forestry practices to all forested regions.
events.supporting_text: Period: 1990s. Response: Expansion of CBF across all regions

significance.justification: Geographic scaling indicates the capacity for CBF to transform forest governance at a systemic level.
significance.supporting_text: Expansion of CBF across all regions

events.title: Growing interest in commercialization of wood and non‑wood goods and services produced under CBF
events.description: Increased focus on market‑oriented production of timber and non‑timber forest products within community‑based forestry systems, driven by globalization and trade liberalization.
events.supporting_text: Period: 2000s Events: Globalization, trade liberalization. Response: Growing interest in commercialization of wood and non‑wood goods and services produced under CBF

significance.justification: Commercial interest suggests a new market‑based pathway that could reshape how CBF contributes to sustainable economies.
significance.supporting_text: Growing interest in commercialization of wood and non‑wood goods and services produced under CBF

events.title: Additions to CBF objectives to address global policy interests (climate change, illegal timber, PES)
events.description: Incorporation of climate‑change mitigation, illegal timber control, and payment‑for‑environmental‑services goals into community‑based forestry objectives, reflecting global policy focus.
events.supporting_text: Period: 2010s Events: Global policy focus on climate change, illegal timber and payment for environmental services Response: Additions to CBF objectives to address global policy interests

significance.justification: Aligning CBF with global climate and anti‑illegal‑timber agendas raises its policy relevance and public legitimacy.
significance.supporting_text: Additions to CBF objectives to address global policy interests (climate change, illegal timber, PES)

events.title: Publication of Ostrom's 1990 narrative on community‑based forestry
events.description: Ostrom’s 1990 work popularized the narrative that local communities with property rights can autonomously manage forest commons sustainably, forming the conceptual basis for community‑based forestry.
events.supporting_text: The popularity of community-based forestry as a formal type of forestry rests primarily on a narrative popularized by Ostrom (1990) that local communities, when granted sufficient property rights over local forest commons, can organize autonomously and develop local institutions to regulate the use of natural resources and manage them sustainably.

significance.justification: The narrative shows that local communities can organize autonomously and develop institutions, enabling collective action.
significance.supporting_text: The popularity ... rests primarily on a narrative ... that local communities, when granted sufficient property rights ... can organize autonomously and develop local institutions

events.title: Publication of Tole 2010 article linking CBF to IMF and World Bank conditionality
events.description: Tole (2010) highlighted that community‑based forestry initiatives align with broader economy‑wide and institutional reforms promoted by IMF and World Bank lending conditions since the 1990s.
events.supporting_text: Tole (2010, p. 1312) noted that CBF initiatives "fit squarely within the larger economy wide and institutional reforms that many governments have been pursuing under IMF [International Monetary Fund] and World Bank conditionality lending since the 1990s.

significance.justification: The article links CBF to economy‑wide reforms under IMF/World Bank conditionality, highlighting prevailing macro‑economic pressures.
significance.supporting_text: CBF initiatives “fit squarely within the larger economy wide and institutional reforms ... under IMF ... and World Bank conditionality"

events.title: Adoption of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples
events.description: The UN adopted the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, providing additional impetus to community‑based forestry movements by emphasizing indigenous peoples’ rights to control traditional natural resources.
events.supporting_text: The United Nations (UN) Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (adopted by the UN in 2007) has given additional impetus to this movement.

significance.justification: UN adoption gave additional legitimacy and momentum to the CBF movement.
significance.supporting_text: The United Nations (UN) Declaration ... has given additional impetus to this movement.

events.title: Establishment of RECOFTC (Regional Center for Forestry Research and Development)
events.description: RECOFTC was founded in Bangkok to focus on capacity‑building for community‑based forestry in Asia and the Pacific.
events.supporting_text: RECOFTC was established in 1987 in Bangkok to provide a focus on capacity building for CBF in Asia and the Pacific.

significance.justification: RECOFTC was created to build capacity for CBF, supporting implementation.
significance.supporting_text: RECOFTC ... provide a focus on capacity building for CBF in Asia and the Pacific.

events.title: FAO Review of Community‑Based Forestry (FAO, 1991)
events.description: FAO published a review of community‑based forestry, marking an early milestone in documenting the state of CBF programmes worldwide.
events.supporting_text: The two previous FAO reviews of CBF (FAO, 1991; Arnold, 2001) provide little in the way of quantitative or even qualitative data on the extent or effectiveness of community forestry.

significance.justification: The review highlighted slow implementation and lack of political will, exposing barriers.
significance.supporting_text: Both of these reviews noted the relatively slow pace of implementation ... a general lack of political will

events.title: Arnold Review of Community‑Based Forestry (Arnold, 2001)
events.description: Arnold’s 2001 review evaluated 25 years of community‑based forestry, calling for a shift from promotion to critical analysis and consolidation.
events.supporting_text: Arnold (2001), in reviewing progress with CBF over the previous 25 years, noted that "it could be desirable if there were now to be a period of consolidation, moving from promotion to critical analysis, with increased consideration of how best to address weaknesses and problems that have arisen".

significance.justification: Arnold called for critical analysis and addressing weaknesses, indicating a shift toward systemic improvement.
significance.supporting_text: it could be desirable ... moving from promotion to critical analysis, with increased consideration of how best to address weaknesses

events.title: Emergence of Institutional Responses to Community‑Based Forestry
events.description: During the late 1980s and 1990s, a series of institutional responses—such as FAO’s Forests, Trees and People Programme, the Social Forestry Network, and other capacity‑building initiatives—were launched to support and disseminate community‑based forestry practices.
events.supporting_text: Institutional response Several institutional responses to the growing importance of CBF emerged in the late 1980s and 1990s.

significance.justification: New institutions (FTPP, Social Forestry Network, RECOFTC) created platforms and networks to support CBF.
significance.supporting_text: FAO’s Forests, Trees and People Programme ... was an important platform for developing and supporting networks

events.title: United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (Rio Earth Summit)
events.description: The 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development, held in Rio de Janeiro, led the Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD) to endorse the role of local communities, indigenous peoples and other stakeholders in pursuing sustainable forest management (SFM).
events.supporting_text: Following the United Nations Conference on the Environment and Development in 1992, the Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD) endorsed the role of local communities, indigenous peoples and other stakeholders in pursuing SFM.

significance.justification: The summit set the stage for later policy actions that re‑orient forest management toward community involvement.
significance.supporting_text: Following the United Nations Conference on the Environment and Development in 1992, the Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD) endorsed the role of local communities...

events.title: Initiation of the Intergovernmental Panel on Forests (IPF)
events.description: The Commission on Sustainable Development (CSD) launched the Intergovernmental Panel on Forests (IPF) to seek a global consensus for action supportive of participatory and sustainable forest management.
events.supporting_text: CSD initiated the Intergovernmental Panel on Forests (IPF) in 1995 to seek a global consensus for action supportive of participatory and sustainable forest management.

significance.justification: IPF was created to build a global consensus supporting participatory and sustainable forest management.
significance.supporting_text: CSD initiated the Intergovernmental Panel on Forests (IPF) in 1995 to seek a global consensus for action supportive of participatory and sustainable forest management.

events.title: Establishment of IUCN Working Group on Community Involvement in Forest Management
events.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) created a Working Group focused on community involvement in forest management and produced a series of five regional reports and a summary document.
actors: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
events.supporting_text: Commencing in 1996, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) established a Working Group on Community Involvement in Forest Management and produced a series of five regional reports ... plus a summary document (Poffenberger, 1996).

significance.justification: The Working Group produced reports that were used to advocate for community‑based forestry internationally.
significance.supporting_text: In 1996, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) established a Working Group on Community Involvement in Forest Management and produced a series of five regional reports.

events.title: Advocacy for Community‑Based Forestry through IUCN Reports
events.description: Between 1996 and 2000 the IUCN regional reports were used to advocate for community‑based forest management in international discussions, providing input to the IPF and its successor, the Intergovernmental Forum on Forests (IFF).
actors: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
events.supporting_text: These were used between 1996 and 2000 to advocate for CBF in international discussions on forests through input to IPF and its successor, the Intergovernmental Forum on Forests (IFF).

significance.justification: The reports were explicitly used to push CBF onto the international forest policy agenda.
significance.supporting_text: These were used between 1996 and 2000 to advocate for CBF in international discussions on forests through input to IPF and its successor, the Intergovernmental Forum on Forests (IFF).

events.title: Launch of UNFF Multi‑Year Programme of Work (2007‑2015)
events.description: The United Nations Forum on Forests (UNFF) incorporated the IPF/IFF Proposals for Action into its Multi‑Year Programme of Work, whose 2007‑2015 cycle highlighted community‑based forest management as a major theme.
events.supporting_text: The successor to IPF and IFF, the United Nations Forum on Forests (UNFF), incorporated the IPF/IFF Proposals for Action into its Multi‑Year Programme of Work. Among the major themes of the 2007−2015 Programme of Work were community‑based forest management...

significance.justification: Embedding CBF as a major theme raised its visibility within the UN forest system.
significance.supporting_text: The United Nations Forum on Forests (UNFF) incorporated the IPF/IFF Proposals for Action into its Multi-Year Programme of Work... major themes... community-based forest management.

events.title: Adoption of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
events.description: In September 2015 the United Nations adopted a set of 17 Sustainable Development Goals, providing a global policy framework that emphasizes integration of economic, social and environmental dimensions and highlights the role of community‑based forestry in achieving SDG 15.2.
events.supporting_text: In September 2015 the United Nations adopted a set of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) which provide an overarching policy framework to guide the world's development agenda until 2030 (UN, 2015).

significance.justification: The agenda creates a global policy framework that can scale up CBF and link it to broader sustainability targets.
significance.supporting_text: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development offers a real opportunity to support the scaling-up of CBF worldwide and enhance its effectiveness.

events.title: International Payment for Environmental Services (PES) Forum
events.description: An international PES forum held in 2014 concluded that most PES schemes were small‑scale and had not met expectations regarding deforestation reduction, income generation, or competitiveness of sustainable forest management.
events.supporting_text: A conclusion from an international PES forum held in 2014 noted that most PES schemes have been small in scale and, by and large, have not fulfilled the expectations that have been claimed for them...

significance.justification: The forum highlighted that most PES schemes have been small and have not met expectations, signalling limited progress.
significance.supporting_text: A conclusion from an international PES forum held in 2014 noted that most PES schemes have been small in scale and, by and large, have not fulfilled the expectations...

events.title: Founding of the Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC)
events.description: The Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC) was established as an international umbrella organization to provide independent assessment, endorsement and recognition of national forest certification systems, especially for small, family‑owned and community forests.
actors: Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC)
events.supporting_text: The Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC) was founded in 1999 in response to the specific requirements of small, family‑owned and community forests as an international umbrella organization...

significance.justification: PEFC was created to address certification needs of small and community forests, facilitating market access.
significance.supporting_text: The Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC) was founded in 1999 in response to the specific requirements of small, family‑owned and community forests.

events.title: Adoption of the EU Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade (FLEGT) Action Plan
events.description: The European Union adopted the Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade (FLEGT) Action Plan, establishing a process centred on Voluntary Partnership Agreements (VPAs) with timber‑exporting countries to ensure legally harvested timber.
events.supporting_text: Concerns about the impact of illegal logging and associated trade led the European Union (EU) to adopt the Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade (FLEGT) Action Plan in 2003.

significance.justification: FLEGT introduced a governance mechanism that could reshape timber legality and affect community forest dynamics.
significance.supporting_text: The EU’s FLEGT process is centred on Voluntary Partnership Agreements... it is widely recognized that tenure insecurity is often a cause of illegal logging activities.

events.title: Signing of Six FLEGT Voluntary Partnership Agreements
events.description: By 2014, the EU had signed Voluntary Partnership Agreements with six timber‑exporting countries, advancing the FLEGT process and creating mechanisms for legal timber trade.
events.supporting_text: As of 2014, FLEGT VPAs had been signed with six countries and others were being negotiated (Saunders, 2014).

significance.justification: High compliance costs risk marginalising small community actors, limiting the benefits of the agreements for them.
significance.supporting_text: However, as with REDD or REDD+ initiatives, compliance costs may be too high for small groups, resulting in their increased marginalization and exclusion from export markets.

events.title: Establishment of the FLARE Network (Forests and Livelihoods: Assessment, Research and Engagement)
events.description: In early 2015 the International Forestry Research Institute (IFRI) announced the creation of the FLARE network, a community of practice aimed at advancing knowledge on forest‑based livelihoods and supporting monitoring and policy development.
events.supporting_text: In early 2015 IFRI announced the establishment of the Forests and Livelihoods: Assessment, Research and Engagement (FLARE) network, a community of practice with the aim of advancing the state of knowledge regarding forest‑based livelihoods.

significance.justification: FLARE creates a community of practice to share knowledge and improve forest‑livelihood interventions globally.
significance.supporting_text: The FLARE network ... aim to advance the state of knowledge regarding forest‑based livelihoods... generate usable information... improve monitoring efforts and efficacy of forest‑dependent livelihood interventions.

events.title: Adoption of multi-point declaration on collective action by indigenous and local communities
events.description: At its eleventh session, the United Nations Forum on Forests (UNFF) adopted a multi‑point declaration that recognized the importance of collective action by indigenous and local communities in advancing sustainable forest management.
events.supporting_text: In the multi-point declaration adopted at its eleventh session, UNFF (2015) recognized the importance of collective action by indigenous and local communities in advancing sustainable forest management.

significance.justification: The declaration explicitly recognises collective action, enabling coordinated community efforts for sustainable forest management.
significance.supporting_text: UNFF (2015) recognized the importance of collective action by indigenous and local communities in advancing sustainable forest management.

events.title: CPF call for increased community role in forest management
events.description: The Collaborative Partnership on Forests (CPF) issued a call for governments worldwide to increase the role of communities in forest management.
events.supporting_text: The Collaborative Partnership on Forests (CPF, 2011) called for governments across the globe to increase the role of communities in forest management.

significance.justification: The call urges governments to expand community participation, building capacity for joint forest stewardship.
significance.supporting_text: The Collaborative Partnership on Forests (CPF, 2011) called for governments across the globe to increase the role of communities in forest management.

events.title: CIFOR strategic plan 2008–2018 research domain on smallholder and community forestry
events.description: The Center for International Forestry Research (CIFOR) incorporated "Improving livelihoods through smallholder and community forestry" as one of six research domains in its strategic plan covering 2008‑2018.
events.supporting_text: The Center for International Forestry Research (CIFOR, 2008) has included "Improving livelihoods through smallholder and community forestry" as one of the six research domains in its 2008−2018 strategic plan.

significance.justification: Identifying research on smallholder forestry highlights pathways for systemic livelihood and ecological improvements.
significance.supporting_text: CIFOR ... has included “Improving livelihoods through smallholder and community forestry” as one of the six research domains in its 2008−2018 strategic plan.

events.title: ITTO inclusion of Community Forest Management and Enterprises in thematic programme
events.description: The International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO) added Community Forest Management and Enterprises as one of its five thematic programmes.
events.supporting_text: The International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO, 2014) has included Community Forest Management and Enterprises as one of its five thematic programmes.

significance.justification: Embedding community forest management in ITTO’s programme signals a shift toward market‑based support for community enterprises.
significance.supporting_text: ITTO (2014) has included Community Forest Management and Enterprises as one of its five thematic programmes.

events.title: CBD COP adoption of target to integrate traditional knowledge into Convention implementation
events.description: The Conference of the Parties (COP) of the Convention on Biological Diversity adopted a target, within its 2011‑2020 strategic plan, to respect and fully integrate traditional knowledge and practices of indigenous and local communities related to the sustainable use of biodiversity.
actors: Conference of the Parties of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
events.supporting_text: The Conference of the Parties of the Convention on Biological Diversity has adopted a target under one of the five goals of its 2011−2020 strategic plan involving respecting and fully integrating traditional knowledge and practices of indigenous and local communities related to sustainable use of biodiversity into the implementation of the Convention (CBD, 2010).

significance.justification: Adopting the target elevates traditional knowledge within an international treaty, increasing its legitimacy.
significance.supporting_text: The COP of CBD has adopted a target ... respecting and fully integrating traditional knowledge and practices of indigenous and local communities.

events.title: FAO revamp of community‑based forestry programme under new Strategic Framework
events.description: Through its new Strategic Framework, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) began revamping its community‑based forestry programme to support its five Strategic Objectives, including rural poverty alleviation, food security, and sustainable provision of natural‑resource goods and services.
events.supporting_text: FAO, through its new Strategic Framework, is revamping its programme on community-based forestry to contribute to its five Strategic Objectives, in particular to rural poverty alleviation, food security and nutrition and the sustainable provision of goods and services from natural resources (FAO, 2013).

significance.justification: FAO’s programme redesign mobilises resources and coordination to strengthen community‑based forestry actions.
significance.supporting_text: FAO, through its new Strategic Framework, is revamping its programme on community‑based forestry to contribute to its five Strategic Objectives.
